business_model.basis: stated in P1 (Item 4.B Business Overview) and F2 (income statement line item)
business_model.claim: ZIM is a global container liner shipping company that earns revenue primarily from transporting cargo in containers across international trade routes.
quotes: We are a global container liner shipping company with leadership positions in niche markets where we believe we have distinct competitive advantages that allow us to maximize our market position and profitability.

business_model.claim: ZIM serves approximately 30,500 customers worldwide, with its 10 largest customers representing about 12% of freight revenues and its 50 largest about 27%.
quotes: We have a highly diverse and global customer base with approximately 30,500 customers (which considers each of our customer entities separately, including in instances where the entity is a subsidiary or branch of another customer, or on a non-consolidated basis) using our services.
In 2025, our 10 largest customers represented approximately 12% of our freight revenues and our 50 largest customers represented approximately 27% of our freight revenues.

business_model.claim: ZIM's operations are organized across five geographic trade zones: Transpacific (43.0%), Intra-Asia (21.2%), Atlantic (13.5%), Latin America (14.4%), and Cross Suez (7.9%) of TEUs carried.
quotes: These trade zones include (for the year ended December 31, 2025, of carried TEUs): (1) Transpacific (43.0%), (2) Atlantic (13.5%), (3) Cross Suez (7.9%), (4) Intra-Asia (21.2%) and (5) Latin America (14.4%).

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5, Factors affecting our results of operations)
business_model.claim: ZIM's revenue is driven by two primary variables: the volume of cargo carried (TEUs) and the average freight rate per TEU, both of which are subject to significant market volatility.
quotes: The volume of cargo that we carry affects our income and profitability from voyages and related services and varies significantly between voyages that depart from, or return to, a port of origin.
Freight rates are largely established by the freight market and we have a limited influence over these rates.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (Item 4.B) and P3 (Item 5, Vessel charter portfolio)
business_model.claim: ZIM chartered-in approximately 86.4% of its TEU capacity and 87.5% of its 128 vessels as of December 31, 2025, owning only 16 vessels, making it highly exposed to charter-market rates.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we operated a fleet of 128 vessels and chartered-in approximately 86.4% of our TEU capacity and 87.5% of the vessels in our fleet.
on December 31, 2025, we owned a total of 16 vessels of our operated fleet, including one vessel we already previously owned prior to these acquisitions

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5, Factors affecting our operating expenses and costs of services)
business_model.claim: ZIM's operating expenses and cost of services in FY2025 were dominated by cargo handling (47.1%), bunker/fuel (25.7%), and port/canal expenses (11.4%).
quotes: Cargo handling accounted for 47.1%, 44.6% and 43.0% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.
Our bunker expenses accounted for 25.7%, 28.5% and 28.3% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
Our port (including canal) expenses accounted for 11.4%, 10.2% and 12.9% of our operating expenses and cost of services for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.claim: In addition to container shipping, ZIM operates 13 chartered car carrier vessels westbound from Asia and runs asset-light logistics subsidiaries providing land transportation, customs brokerage, LCL, project cargo, and air freight in multiple countries.
quotes: In addition to containerized cargo, we also transport vehicles (such as cars, buses and trucks) via dedicated car carrier vessels westbound from Asia, and primarily from China, Japan and South Korea. Currently, we charter thirteen car carrier vessels

These subsidiaries, which we operate, among others, in China, Canada, Brazil, India, Singapore, Hong Kong and the U.S, are asset-light and provide services such as land transportation, custom brokerage, LCL, project cargo and air freight services.

P3.s24.text: Container freight rates were generally lower than in 2024, indicating easing rates for much of the year, though volatility persisted due to ongoing political risks, including continues Red Sea crisis.

P3.s61.text: Charter hire rates in 2025 have moderately increased with similar charter periods on average compared to 2024 In addition, according to Alphaliner, global container ship capacity is expected to increase by 3.7% in 2026, with deliveries of 1.4 million TEUs out of a vessel order book of 11.3 million TEU, while demand for shipping services is projected to increase only by 2.5%.
